summary: Everyone takes CLASSICS 150, which is both the WIM course and the capstone, and completes one subplan: Classical Studies, Ancient History, Greek, Latin, or Greek and Latin (65 units). Each subplan's listed requirements are checked, and its CLASSICS electives make up the rest of the 60 units. Every course must be letter graded with a C or better, and at most 10 units of CLASSICS 198 directed reading and at most 10 units of CLASSICS 199 honors research count. You check by hand courses the Director of Undergraduate Studies approves (300-level graduate courses, repeated language courses, other courses for the Ancient History requirements), that AP or placement credit is not counted, and for honors CLASSICS 199, the 3.6 GPA in the major and the thesis.

program.why: Grading: "All courses taken for the major and minor must be completed with a letter grade. Courses receiving a grade lower than a C will not be considered toward fulfilling major or minor requirements."

totals.label: CLASSICS 198 directed reading
totals.why: Policies: "Enrollment in the independent study section (CLASSICS198 Directed Readings) requires prior approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies. A maximum of three enrollments, totaling no more than 10 units, may be counted toward the major." The 10-unit cap is checked; the three-enrollment limit is left to the DUS approval each enrollment needs.

totals.label: CLASSICS 199 honors thesis

node.name: Further CLASSICS courses toward the 65 units

add.why: Block notes: "Greek and Latin subplan: 65 total units required." Latin and Greek ask for 30 units each; the rest of the 65 (the block floor) comes from further courses, "Recommended additional coursework in Biblical Greek, Sanskrit, or Ancient History". "Sanskrit may be counted toward the degree only if Greek and Latin requirements are fulfilled with coursework at the intermediate level and above", so Sanskrit is moved in by hand.
"GPA Requirement: A minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.6 within the major is required"
